subject: Fleet boundary and deletion certification request — FinTrust Dedicated
messages:
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@fintrust.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.example
Cc: compliance@fintrust.com
Date: Thu, 9 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated deployment - firm boundary / deletion evidence needed

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo this week. As we continue through procurement we have two compliance checkpoints we need to close before Legal will finalize the SOW:

1) Confirmation that the Dedicated capacity for FinTrust will be bound to a single legal territory (US) with no cross-region snapshot replication or asynchronous replication out of that territory.
2) Clear artifacts that prove wipe / deletion of tenant data (including ephemeral caches and backups) within X hours after the retention window or at termination. We need the timeline, owners, and sample artifacts you can provide as evidence.

On retention: our baseline requirement is 90 days of transactional logs and 30 days for request-level KV caches; we also need confirmation of deletion sequencing for backups/snapshots and whether cold copies are ever stored outside the pinned region.

If you have a concise checklist or a topological diagram that shows where data lives and which flows we can use for our audit, that would speed this up.

Can you loop in whoever owns the topology and the legal attestation?

Best,
Rajiv
Rajiv Patel
Head of Cloud Compliance
FinTrust Corporation

Ask (concise):
- Topology diagram (PDF): show tenant compute, ephemeral caches, snapshot stores, and backup lifecycle. Highlight region pin and any services that touch metadata.
- Snapshot & backup policy: how snapshots are stored and deleted; confirm no cross-region replication for this tenant.
- KMS scope & key residency: confirm KMS keys can be customer-scoped and restricted to US KMS regions.
- Purge runbook & proof artifacts: list of logs/events we will capture (storage delete markers, snapshot deletion events, audit log entries with timestamps).
- Retention summary: confirm we can meet 90/30 day buckets and provide the retention enforcement mechanism.

Also, if there are any small showstoppers (dependencies on cloud provider features, inevitable meta-replication) call them out. We need an honest set of limitations rather than a gloss.

Thanks — Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>

Jordan / Kim —

Attaching the topology diagram and a short technical Q&A. High-level confirmations below (more detail in the PDF):

- Region lock: Dedicated clusters can be pinned to a single AWS region (we use placement groups and tenancy constraints). No automated snapshot replication to other regions is enabled for pinned tenants.
- Snapshots & backups: We keep snapshot manifests in the same region. We do have a snapshot-archive job (cold archive) which is disabled for region-pinned Dedicated customers by default; for FinTrust it will remain off unless explicitly requested.
- Retention enforcement: Snapshot lifecycle rules are enforced by an opaque orchestrator; deletion operations are recorded in our audit log with object IDs and timestamps. We can provide exemplar delete events from a staging purge.
- KMS & keys: We support customer-managed KMS keys. Keys are created in the desired US KMS region and never exported.
- Purge sequencing: purge flow = terminate compute -> delete ephemeral KV/caches -> delete storage objects -> delete snapshots -> record events -> finalize. Expected end-to-end from trigger to final marker: ~2–8 hours depending on object counts; typical FinTrust estimate 1–3 hours.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-topology.pdf (topology diagram), redwood-geo-qna.txt (short Q&A).

I’ll run a staged purge tomorrow on a non-prod tenant and collect the delete events for packaging. Kim — ping me which logs you want surfaced to the attestation.

Ben Carter
Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Laura has prepared an attestation letter and Kim can provide the audit-log extracts on request; both are ready to be bundled with the DocuSign package once you confirm.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if anything needs clarifying.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
